vertical_attributes.unit_uncertainty: The layer metadata gives no unit annotation for R or floor fields. Values are interpreted as feet because the repeated floor increments and Purdue records are consistent with feet. The model roof height is therefore an estimate (102 ft = 31.09 m), not surveyed height.

sources.uncertainty: Footprint is source-backed. Geographic conversion is a local approximation, not survey control. GIS service does not provide source/edit dates.

sources.provider: Purdue University Archives and Special Collections
sources.feature_id: Ernest C. Young Hall (West Lafayette, Ind.), corporate entity record 656
sources.source_date: Record consulted 2026-10-26; building record gives 1962 construction. Individual photograph dates are not provided.
sources.measurement_method: Archival record states 10 stories, 1962 construction and original use; the downloaded archival exterior photographs directly inform the original long-slab massing, panelized light facade and narrow vertical window rhythm. The record lists limestone as a material.
sources.uncertainty: Historical photographs have no individual capture dates and do not establish the current full exterior; the current Purdue facade detail photo supports only the red-brick sign wall and its finish.

model_edits: Replaced the original one-piece block with a GIS-ring extrusion at the original campus coordinates and stable object/collection names.

Added a ten-level narrow vertical-window rhythm, light exterior panels with vertical facade piers, red-brick entry sign wall, pale trim, recessed entrance, flat roof finish, and a small representative lobby/corridor slice.
Window proportions, entry details, roof treatment and interior layout are visual estimates; no public measured elevations or floor plan were found.

estimated_dimensions.height_basis: GIS R=102, interpreted as feet; not independently surveyed
estimated_dimensions.horizontal_coordinates: Project local equirectangular approximation, campus-world coordinates retained

unresolved: GIS floor count attributes say 11 while Purdue Archives describes 10 stories; likely includes basement, but this is not explicit in the GIS metadata.
GIS vertical values have no unit metadata. The feet interpretation is plausible but remains an inference.
